text: Nier Replicant, Nier Gestalt, Nier The State of Western JRPG Localization circa 2010 was absolutely grim. Square Enix apparently decided the Xbox demographic, and the American demographic for all systems for that matter, couldn't identify with a Japanese teenager experiencing existential despair, so they replaced him with a 47-year-old divorced transmission mechanic whose forehead resembles a GM bellhousing. T56 on the garage floor. 4L60E slipping into third. S10 outside on blocks since 2009. Dad nowhere to be found. Fentanyl afoot. The scum are legion. Meanwhile Japanese players got a young man contemplating the ontological implications of his sister's mortality, the collapse of human civilization, and the metaphysical distinction between soul and consciousness. Americans got a guy who looks like he owes Snap-on $8,400. Same Game. Same existential themes. Just a fundamentally different understanding of the target consumer. And somehow this was considered good market segmentation. The Absolute State of Gaming.
label: analysis

text: Romancing SaGa 1 Minstrel Song Review [Bottom Line Up Front] Romancing SaGa 1 (Minstrel Song Remaster to be exact) has a reputation for being overly complex in some respects and ultimately I think that reputation is well earned. It has a wealth of mechanics and peculiar hurdles that can really diminish the potential for fun but despite that provides an endearing experience worth a playthrough or two. This was a great leap beyond SaGa 3 (FFL3) but in doing so leapt a bit far off the target zone. Even the remaster does not quite align into a fully refined experience so leaves some opportunities for yet another remake in the future. This game has various ways of trying to bring a tabletop experience like Dungeons & Dragons to the JRPG context but it stumbles a bit out of the gate on that. Ultimately it is still worth experiencing with a lot to enjoy.

For the most part, it is a 4 wide grid where you hit falling notes... Story: What brings this all together though.. is its story. Now, while it doesn't do anything especially groundbreaking, its execution is fantastic. To say that it's an emotional rollercoaster would be an understatement.
